title: A Code Cleanup Wants to Destroy the Production Database
intro: A pull request titled 'refactor: move database into a module' passed review. The deploy pipeline's plan step posted its output — and someone noticed it before approving the apply.

steps.prompt: Look at the plan that was posted.
steps.fake_output:
# aws_db_instance.main will be destroyed
# module.database.aws_db_instance.main will be created
Plan: 1 to add, 0 to change, 1 to destroy.
steps.hint: Read every 'destroy' line in a plan. A refactor should never destroy anything.

steps.prompt: Terraform sees the old address as removed and the new module address as brand new. Confirm the existing database's current state address.
steps.hint: The resource is still recorded in state under its old, root-level address.

steps.prompt: Back up state, then move the database's state entry to its new address inside the module.
steps.hint: state mv changes only the address Terraform uses to track it; the database itself is untouched.

steps.prompt: Re-run the plan to confirm the destroy is gone.
steps.fake_output: No changes. Your infrastructure matches the configuration.
steps.hint: A correct refactor ends with zero changes.

resolution: Moving a resource into a module changes its address (aws_db_instance.main became module.database.aws_db_instance.main). Terraform matches resources by address, so it concluded the old database should be destroyed and a new, empty one created — which would have wiped production data. The plan made this visible, but only because someone actually read it. Fixes, in order of preference: (1) put a 'moved { from = aws_db_instance.main, to = module.database.aws_db_instance.main }' block in the same PR, so the refactor is safe by construction and reviewed as code; (2) add 'lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }' to databases and other stateful resources, which makes Terraform refuse any plan that destroys them; (3) have CI fail or require extra approval whenever a plan contains a destroy on production. Any one of these would have stopped this on its own.
